subject: Dedicated capacity: perf targets and sizing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-22T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity: perf targets and sizing follow-up

Thanks Jordan — great conversation today. Quick recap from our end and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on SLOs and sizing for a Dedicated capacity pilot: 

Key perf targets you called out:
- P95 latency (token streaming, 8k context) target: <= 150ms
- P99 latency target: <= 300ms (for non-stream critical paths)
- Concurrency: sustained 200 concurrent user streams (burst to 400 for 2-3 min)
- Average tokens/sec per stream: ~35 tokens/s
- Model: mix of Llama-2-70B and a smaller 13B fallback for cost-sensitive routes; need guidance on quantized vs fp16 for quality

Sizing / dedicated ask:
- You asked for reserved throughput that guarantees above SLOs during business hours (PST 8am-8pm).
- We'll surface two SKU comparisons (A100-80GB vs H100) with # GPUs and expected reserved reqs/s and token throughput.

Attachments sent: shopfast-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (provisional numbers) and benchmarks-a100-vs-h100.pdf (micro-benchmark summaries).

Next steps (proposed):
1) Internal micro-benchmark: Redwood infra team runs a 1-hour sim of 200 sustained streams + bursts on both A100 and H100 configs. (We propose window Thu 3/25 morning PST).
2) Deliver updated sizing sheet with recommended #GPUs, reserved throughput (tokens/s), expected monthly committed spend.
3) Optional pilot: 2-week Dedicated pilot with canary routing and telemetry, followed by a go/no-go.

Can you confirm timing for the micro-benchmark (Thu 3/25 AM PST works on our side) and whether procurement should be looped in now?

Thanks,
Marissa

marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary and thanks for the attachments. A few clarifications from our side: 

- P95 150ms sound right for streaming; can you also quantify P99 for streaming (we care about tail because we show live responses to agents)?
- For concurrency: the 200 concurrent streams are mostly short chat sessions (avg 40 tokens per response) but about 10% are long-running multi-turn sessions with KV cache. How will KV cache affect the throughput numbers?
- For fallback model: can you include expected quality delta (ROUGE or similar) and token-cost delta between 70B fp16 and 13B q4h?

Thu 3/25 AM PST works for the micro-bench. Looping in procurement (procurement@shopfast.com) — they prefer to review any draft SOW before pilot.

If you can also include an estimate for reserved tokens/sec (and how that maps to reserved GPUs) in the sizing spreadsheet that would help speed procurement.

Jordan

Jordan — putting some rough numbers here ahead of the live micro-bench on Thu. These are ballpark based on our prior workloads and the benchmarks attached: 

Quick estimator assumptions:
- Llama-2-70B fp16 on H100 (optimized kernels): ~12 tokens/ms per GPU for streaming steady-state (varies by input length).
- Llama-2-70B q4f16 on A100: ~7-8 tokens/ms per GPU (larger variance).
- KV cache: multi-turn sessions with large context increase memory pressure; effective throughput drops ~10-15% depending on active cache hit rate.

Rough sizing (to meet P95 <=150ms at 200 concurrent streams):
- H100 path: 6x H100 per region reserved (est. sustained tokens/sec ~50k, headroom for bursts to 90k)
- A100 path: 10x A100 per region reserved (est. sustained tokens/sec ~48k, bursts to 70k)
- Fallback 13B q4h can run on smaller nodes; recommend 2-3 GPUs for fallback pool to absorb 20% of traffic during cost mode.

I'll run a focused micro-bench Thursday and post the raw numbers into the sizing sheet. We should capture p50/p95/p99 for both streaming and non-stream endpoints and include CPU/RAM utilization and KV cache hit/miss rates.

Marissa — want me to run the bench at 8:00 AM PST or 10:00 AM PST?

Thanks,
Aditya
